output.text: The robotics workshop began early on a cool Saturday morning with tables full of gears, wires, and small motors waiting to be assembled. Assume that Isla is the lead volunteer. Sami arrived first, carrying a box of spare circuit boards, and set up near the window where the light was best for soldering. Vik came in a few minutes later, greeting everyone with a cheerful wave before finding a seat beside the main workbench. Kai took the photographs. Ben arrived last, slightly out of breath from rushing across campus, and quickly joined the group already gathered around the central table. Sami is in the same study group as Vik. Throughout the morning, the participants worked on programming small wheeled robots to follow a marked path, occasionally pausing to compare their code with one another. Isla stood a little taller than Ben, which made it easy for her to reach the shelf where extra batteries were stored. Vik is not in the same study group as Ben. Kai, meanwhile, moved quietly around the room, adjusting angles and lighting to capture the best shots of the robots in motion. Sami is not in the same study group as Ben. By midafternoon, the youngest participant, Ben, had become the most confident with the soldering iron, while Vik focused on writing clean, efficient code. Sami tested each robot repeatedly, checking wheel alignment and battery levels before every trial run. As the workshop wound down, everyone gathered their tools, comparing notes on what they might build next time, already looking forward to the next session together.
